introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: LLM coding assistants and repair tools are used on security-relevant code, and their outputs come with statements of success that users tend to trust.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: A repair tool's claim that it fixed a vulnerability is not evidence that it did; on real Python vulnerabilities with paired exploit and functional tests (Vul4Py), the rate of unverified positive claims (false assurance) and its relation to the verified repair rate have not been measured for the models and pipelines this project studies. The pilot covers 5 cases and one model only.
search_directions: security of code produced with AI assistants and users' trust in it (Copilot security, users with AI assistants writing less secure code and believing it secure)
automation bias and complacency in human use of automated aids
verbalized confidence and calibration of large language models
surveys of automated program repair and of LLM-based program repair

related_work_strategy.overview: Three clusters: (1) LLM-based vulnerability repair and benchmarks with executable checks; (2) plausible versus correct patches in test-based repair; (3) self-verification by LLMs and LLMs as judges. The project's measurement (claim recorded before an executable oracle) sits between them.

subsections.subsection_title: 2.1 LLM-based vulnerability repair and its benchmarks
subsections.methodology_cluster: Zero-shot and learned vulnerability repair evaluated on datasets of real vulnerabilities with tests or exploits (Vul4J, Vul4Py, PatchEval, VulRepair).
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find the benchmarks and empirical studies that evaluate LLM vulnerability repair with executable checks, up to the cutoff.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Studies report repair rates but rarely compare the model's own claim of success with the executable verdict.
limitation_search_queries: zero-shot vulnerability repair large language models
how effective are neural networks for fixing security vulnerabilities
reproducible vulnerabilities dataset program repair exploit tests
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Record the claim and confidence before running the oracle and report FAR next to VRR.

subsections.methodology_cluster: Test-based (generate-and-validate) program repair and the overfitting of plausible patches.
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find the canonical studies showing that passing tests is not the same as being correct, and patch-correctness assessment work.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Functional tests alone accept patches that do not fix the defect; security needs exploit tests as part of the oracle.
limitation_search_queries: identifying patch correctness test-based program repair
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: A repair counts only when the patch applies, the functional tests still pass and the exploit tests pass.

subsections.methodology_cluster: LLMs that check their own or other models' outputs: self-repair, self-correction, LLM-as-a-judge, judge biases.
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find evidence on how reliable LLM self-assessment and LLM judges are, especially for code.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Self-assessment and same-family judges share errors and favor their own outputs, so they can inflate assurance.
limitation_search_queries: large language models cannot self-correct reasoning
is self-repair a silver bullet for code generation
LLM evaluators recognize and favor their own generations
correlated errors in large language models
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Planned work: a pipeline of three models (analysis, repair, evaluator) whose claims are judged by the same oracle.

content_bullets: One paragraph, about 200 words (MDPI): background (claims of repair are not evidence), methods (Vul4Py oracle, VRR and FAR with Wilson intervals, pilot with poolside/laguna-xs-2.1 on 5 cases), results (VRR 1/5, FAR 3/4 with intervals), conclusions (pilot too small for comparisons; planned study).
Vul4Py: 100 vulnerabilities (92 CVEs, 8 GitHub advisories) in 61 Python projects; vulnerable and fixed commits, functional and exploit tests; commit f80f861.
Verified repair: patch applies, functional tests pass, exploit tests pass; skipped tests never count as passes.
